version: arXiv:1508.04805v1; author-created version of JOTA article, 21 PDF pages

read_ranges.scope: entire paper including all robust reformulations, examples, conclusion and appendices A–B

topic_relevance.A01: direct/adjacent: extends fractional programming to uncertain numerator, denominator and constraints; supplies CCT exact cases and a parametric residual method for the general robust case.

definitions.name: nonrobust fractional program
definitions.statement: min f(x)/g(x), subject to h_i(x)≤0, with convex nonnegative f and concave positive g over feasible X.

definitions.name: Schaible/CCT perspective form
definitions.statement: Set y=x/g(x), t=1/g(x), then minimize t f(y/t) with t g(y/t)≥1 and t h_i(y/t)≤0. With f≥0, replacing equality by ≥1 preserves the optimal value.

definitions.name: robust fractional program (R-FP)
definitions.statement: Minimize α subject to f(a₀,x)/g(a₀,x)≤α for every a₀∈U₀ and h_i(a_i,x)≤0 for every a_i∈U_i; g>0 on all feasible x and uncertainty realizations.

definitions.name: parametric residual F(α)
definitions.statement: F(α)=min_{x,w} w subject to f(a₀,x)−αg(a₀,x)≤w for every a₀ and robust feasibility constraints. Under the stated assumptions it is convexly representable and nonincreasing; its zero identifies the robust ratio value.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.1 (Schaible–Dinkelbach duality)
assumptions: f convex and nonnegative on X
theorem_cards.statement: The Schaible perspective program and the Dinkelbach parameter program are dual, with strong duality.
proof_steps: Rewrite the Dinkelbach program as the largest α whose residual f(x)−αg(x) is nonnegative for every x.
Apply the “primal worst equals dual best” duality result after restricting to a compact box containing an attained optimizer.
For fixed x, dualize the scalar robust constraint; the optimistic counterpart is exactly the Schaible perspective formulation.
A sufficiently large t gives Slater feasibility and strong duality.
gaps: The proof relies on the cited robust minimax duality result; its compactness reduction uses attainment.

theorem_cards.label: Robust special case S1 (independent numerator and denominator uncertainty)
assumptions: The numerator and denominator uncertainty sets are separable/independent
Positive denominator and stated robust convexity assumptions
Nonnegative numerator, unless the denominator is certain and the normalization equality variant applies
theorem_cards.statement: The robust problem is exactly equivalent to the robust counterpart of the Schaible transformation; under generic conjugate duality, it has a tractable formulation for convex uncertainty sets.
proof_steps: Introduce y=x/t and t>0 with separate uncertain numerator and denominator constraints.
The inverse map x=y/t maps feasible solutions both ways.
For the conjugate-based robust counterpart, apply perspective conjugates to each uncertainty-wise constraint.
gaps: Separability of uncertainty is essential for this exact transformation; one cannot replace correlated numerator/denominator uncertainty with independent choices without changing the model.

theorem_cards.label: Robust special case S2 (denominator independent of x)
assumptions: g(a₀) contains no optimization variable x
Convex uncertainty sets and robust conjugate assumptions
theorem_cards.statement: The robust ratio problem is equivalent to the robust inequality f(a₀,x)−αg(a₀)≤0 and can be reformulated as a convex optimization problem.
proof_steps: Since g does not depend on x, multiply by the positive denominator without introducing x-dependent products.
Use the robust conjugate representation for the resulting inequalities.
gaps: This case is narrow and does not handle a decision-dependent denominator.

theorem_cards.label: General robust-root method
assumptions: Compact robust feasible set in x

Assumptions (a)–(g): compact convex uncertainty sets; convexity/concavity in x and uncertain parameters as stated; positive denominator; numerator nonnegative for some numerator realization (unless biaffine exceptions apply)
theorem_cards.statement: Solve the monotone residual F(α)=0 by bisection or a Dinkelbach-type method, where each residual evaluation is a convex robust optimization problem; exact roots give an exact robust optimum, and convergent root sequences yield optimal solutions under cited compactness results.
proof_steps: At fixed α≥0 the robust residual constraints are convex under the parameter-curvature assumptions.
Positive g makes F nonincreasing in α; sign bounds bracket the unique threshold α*.
Bisection halves the bracket per residual sign evaluation.
The authors summarize Dinkelbach-type alternatives and the condition under which convergent primal subsequences recover an optimizer.
gaps: No universal finite iteration count or root-finding rate is asserted for the general method; compactness and robust-convexity assumptions cannot be omitted.

constant_dependence.explicit: Bisection gives interval-width reduction by 1/2 per iteration. For root accuracy δ from initial width W, this yields ⌈log₂(W/δ)⌉ residual solves. The residual subproblem dimension and tractability depend on uncertainty-set conjugates and number of robust constraints.
constant_dependence.dependence: The paper reports example timings (e.g. 37 bisection iterations in its mean-variance example) but does not give a general computational bound for conic representation size.

endpoint_limits.denominator: Strict positivity for every feasible x and every allowed numerator/denominator realization is required before ratio inequalities can be multiplied through.
endpoint_limits.uncertainty: Convex compact uncertainty regions are required by the generic RO method; the paper notes convexity can be dropped in special finite-scenario/S-lemma/SOS cases.
endpoint_limits.sign: Nonnegative numerator supports α≥0 and convex parametric residual; biaffine denominators give specified exceptions.
endpoint_limits.exchange: The paper only exchanges max/min in an Sion setting with quasi-convex/quasi-concave continuity, convex feasible X and compact convex uncertainty set; uncertainty in constraints changes feasible X and breaks that conclusion.

reusable_methods.method: Normalize a positive fractional objective using the perspective lift
reusable_methods.transfer: Preserve a single shared input and exact inverse map. For a maximal-cube application with multiple uncertain or jointly chosen cubes, add common-selection constraints; the paper’s separable robust special case does not license independent cube choices.

reusable_methods.method: Convert a ratio threshold into a parametric residual sign test
reusable_methods.transfer: At fixed α, certify f−αg≤0 over the full feasible domain; use bisection with validated lower/upper brackets. This is useful when the robust ratio model is convex but no one-shot CCT is available.
Transform uncertainty constraints only after verifying convexity/concavity in both decision variables and uncertain parameters, uncertainty compactness, and conjugate domains.
